raw.cause: logger's channel is created with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY (event -20327001, flags 0x4b), so when logger receives display's MsgSend it keeps its own priority 10 instead of inheriting display's 30. media's priority-20 busy loops then occupy both CPUs. logger sits READY (105809) while media runs (105820, 104932), and its 2 ms log write stretches to about 47 ms (105796→109142). display (priority 30) stays REPLY-blocked the whole time; the same pattern recurs at 103068→103176, 113574→115210 and 119323→119077.
raw.qnx_call: ChannelCreate with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY in logger (the channel display MsgSends to)
raw.fix_summary: Drop _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY from the logger channel so the receiving thread inherits display's priority 30 while it serves the message; it then preempts media and replies in about 2 ms. If the goal is that logging never competes with real work, make the log path non-blocking instead (a pulse, or a queue drained by a low-priority thread). Do not keep a synchronous MsgSend to a fixed-low-priority server.

finding: display waits on logger behind lower priority work
